@graph.headline: Spring Fence Prep: Getting Your Michigan Wood Fence Ready After Winter
@graph.description: A complete spring fence inspection and maintenance checklist for Michigan homeowners. Learn how to assess winter damage, repair wood fences, and protect your investment for years to come.

mainEntity.name: When should I inspect my fence in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: April is ideal. The snow has melted, the ground is soft enough to identify post movement, and you have time to schedule repairs before the summer rush. Do a second quick check in September before winter.

mainEntity.name: What damage does Michigan winter cause to wood fences?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main culprits are freeze-thaw cycles that loosen joints, frost heave that tilts posts, ice buildup at post bases that causes rot, snow drifts that bend panels, and wind that cracks boards.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to stain a fence in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: July and August. The wood is dry, the humidity is low, and the stain will absorb and cure properly. Avoid staining in spring when the wood is still saturated from snowmelt, or in fall when temperatures drop too quickly for proper curing.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my fence needs repair or full replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: If fewer than 25% of boards are damaged and the posts are solid, repairs make sense. If posts are rotted or leaning, or if multiple sections are failing, replacement is usually more cost-effective in the long run.

mainEntity.name: Can I repair my fence myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many maintenance tasks — tightening hardware, replacing individual boards, staining — are DIY-friendly. Post replacement, structural repairs, and new installations are best left to professionals, especially in Michigan's challenging soil conditions.

mainEntity.name: How much does fence repair cost in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minor repairs (a few boards, hardware) typically run $100-$500. Post replacement costs $200-$400 per post including concrete. Full section replacement runs $1,500-$3,000 depending on length and materials.
